footer.credit: Built for process-mining research at University of Augsburg.

single_run.intro_content: In a Single Run you execute exactly one algorithm on exactly one log — the simplest setup to get started. This walkthrough highlights the key spots; ESC or Skip exits at any time.
single_run.algo_pick_content: On the left you find the available tools, grouped by category. Clicking an entry selects it.
single_run.algo_help_content: Next to every algorithm sits a ? icon. Clicking it opens a panel with a detailed explanation — what the algorithm does, how it works, when to use it.
single_run.logsource_content: Two sources for the log: 'Upload File' for your own XES or JSON files (recent uploads are listed below), or 'Use Sample' for the bundled example log.
single_run.params_content: Every tool has its own parameters with sensible defaults. The preset bar above lets you save and reuse configurations — also in Batch.
single_run.run_content: Once algorithm + log + parameters fit, run via Ctrl/Cmd+Enter or click. The result appears inline with stats, tables, plots and downloads. Past runs land in the jobs panel on the right.

batch.intro_content: In Batch mode ONE algorithm runs over up to 10 logs at once. Errors on individual logs don't stop the rest. This walkthrough highlights the key spots; ESC or Skip exits at any time.
batch.algo_content: Pick the algorithm that will run across all logs. Next to it sits a ? icon for a detailed explanation.
batch.logs_content: Mix up to 10 logs from your own uploads, recent uploads and sample logs. Selected logs appear in the Selected section.
batch.params_content: The tool runs with the same parameters across every selected log, so the results are comparable.
batch.run_content: Run via Ctrl/Cmd+Enter or click. Progress streams live per log; on errors the other runs keep going. The result is a table with status + stats per log.

onboarding.step0_p1: Discover process models from event logs and measure how complex they are, right in the browser. No install, no command line — drop in a log and run.
onboarding.step0_p2: This quick tour shows the four things you'll use most.
onboarding.step1_title: Pick an algorithm and a log
onboarding.step1_p1: Choose a tool from the left sidebar. Then either upload your own event log or pick a sample log or a recently uploaded one.
onboarding.step1_p2: Tip: once a log is selected, an overview of its traces, variants and activities appears above the parameters.
onboarding.step2_p1: Hit 'Run analysis'. Progress streams live; when the run finishes you get every artifact inline — stats, tables, process models, downloadable logs — plus a one-click 'Download All (ZIP)'.
onboarding.step2_p2: Past runs stay in the jobs archive on the right, so you can re-open them anytime.
onboarding.step3_title: Power features when you need them
onboarding.step3_batch: Batch — run one algorithm over up to 10 logs at once; failures don't stop the rest.
onboarding.step3_api: API — drive everything from Python or curl; see the API page in the header for examples.
onboarding.step3_history: History — every run of your session stays available in the jobs panel and on the runs page.
